figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Radical-mediated enzymatic carbon−carbon/heteroatom
cross-linking in RiPPs. (A) rSAM-catalyzed His-Tyr cross-linking in
dynobactin. (B) P450-catalyzed His-Tyr cross-linking in biarylitide.
(C) BURP-catalyzed Gly-Trp cross-linking in legumenin. (D) MNIO-
catalyzed 5-thio-oxazole formation in bufferin. (E) This work: αKGD-
catalyzed Cys-Tyr cross-linking in corsin.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Bioinformatic analysis of bacterial αKGDs and their existence in RiPP BGCs. (A) Sequence similarity network (SSN) of InterPro Family
IPR003347 (JmjC domain-containing proteins, JMJDs) in bacteria. Functional characterized JMJDs including EcYcfD, RmYcfD and PoyI are
marked in the map. Clusters containing BGCs encoding both JMJD homologues and class II lanthipeptide synthetases are also highlighted in the
map. (B) Genome neighborhood networks (GNNs) of DUF4135 (class II lanthipeptide dehydratase domain) to retrieve putative RiPPs-related
gene clusters. (C) The conserved genomic content of BGC candidates. (D) Sequence logo of the C-terminal 15 amino acids of precursor peptide
candidates. Conserved residues are marked with red triangles.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Biosynthetic gene cluster and chemical structure of the copper-binding bicyclic lanthipeptide corsin. (A) The putative cor BGC from S.
corchorusii. (B) The chemical structure of corsin elucidated by NMR. The 2D NMR correlations of the MeLan and the Cys-Tyr cross-link are
shown. (C) UV−Vis spectra of a CAS-Cu(II) solution titrated by corsin. Assay conditions: a solution of 200 μM CAS, 400 μM HDTMA and 22
μM CuSO4 in 25 mM HEPES buffer (pH 7.5) was titrated by corsin and incubated for 10 min before analyzed by a UV−Vis spectrometer. (D)
MALDI-TOF-MS spectra of the samples of corsin with CuSO4.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Coexpression of His6-tagged CorA with CorM, CorB and
CorD in E. coli BL21. The resulting products were digested by GluC
and analyzed by MALDI-TOF-MS.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. In vitro reconstitution of enzymatic activities of CorM, CorB and CorD. (A) MALDI-TOF-MS analysis of in vitro modification of CorA
by CorM and CorB-CorD. Assay conditions for CorM modification: 100 μM peptide substrate, 10 μM CorM, 10 mM ATP, 10 mM MgCl2, 50 mM
HEPES, pH 8.0, 25 °C, 2 h. Assay conditions for CorB and CorD modification: 100 μM peptide substrate, 10 μM CorB, 10 μM CorD, 100 μM
Fe2+, 200 μM α-ketoglutarate, 100 μM ascorbate, 50 mM HEPES, pH 8.0, 25 °C, 2 h. (B) MALDI-TOF-MS analysis of in vitro modification of
CorAMeLan‑((−3)‑9) by CorB and CorD. CorAMeLan‑CY‑((−3)‑9) was prepared by GluC digestion of CorAMeLan.

figure_candidates.caption: Table 1. Modification of CorA Mutants by CorM, CorB, and CorD via Co-expression in E. colia

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. Mechanism investigation of CorB-CorD-catalyzed Cys-Tyr cross-linking. (A) Two possible mechanisms of Cys-Tyr cross-linking. (B)
MALDI-TOF-MS analysis of CorB-CorD-modified CorAMeLan in D2O and H2O after protease K digestion. Assay conditions: 100 μM CorAMeLan,
10 μM CorB, 10 μM CorD, 100 μM Fe2+, 200 μM α-ketoglutarate, 100 μM ascorbate, 50 mM HEPES, pH 8.0, 25 °C, 2h. (C) Trapping of the
pQM intermediate generated during the modification of CorA by CorB and CorD. Assay conditions: 100 μM CorA, 10 μM CorB, 10 μM CorD,
100 μM Fe2+, 200 μM α-ketoglutarate, 100 μM ascorbate, 1 mM βME, 50 mM HEPES, pH 8.0, 25 °C, 8h.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. In vitro modification of CorAY7F‑MeLan by CorB-CorD. (A) Modification of CorAY7F‑MeLan by CorB-CorD generated CorAY7F‑MeLan‑hydroxyl.
(B) MALDI-TOF-MS analysis of in vitro modification of CorAY7F‑MeLan by CorB-CorD. Assay conditions: 100 μM CorAY7F‑MeLan, 10 μM CorB, 10
μM CorD, 100 μM Fe2+, 200 μM α-ketoglutarate, 100 μM ascorbate, 50 mM HEPES, pH 8.0, 25 °C, 2h. CorAY7F‑MeLan was obtained by
coexpression of CorAY7F with CorM in E. coli BL21. (C) HR-MS/MS spectra of desulfurized CorAY7F‑MeLan‑hydroxyl after GluC digestion
(CorAY7F‑MeLan‑hydroxyl‑linearized‑((−3)‑9)).
